description: Verify that DUT silently discards an IPv4 packet whose Destination Address is neither one of its own addresses nor a broadcast / multicast address — strict accept-list per RFC 1122 §3.2.1.3
approach:
[Objective]
A host must drop traffic addressed to neither itself nor a group it belongs to — otherwise it would forward (which a host MUST NOT) or generate spurious responses. This case sends an Echo Request with dst_ip pointing at some other unicast address and confirms DUT stays silent.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 packet to dst_ip = (some other host's IP, not DUT, not broadcast, not multicast)

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any response.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT responded despite the wrong dst_ip. Indicates DUT is acting as a router (forbidden for hosts) or its accept-list is too permissive.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the cross-addressed packet — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT responded to a packet not addressed to it — accept-list too permissive
